newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock up on speculation of Buffett interest.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock up on speculation of Buffett interest.

text.p: Nike Inc. stock rallied for the second straight session Wednesday as Wall Street speculated that billionaire investor Warren Buffett favours the sports marketing giant as an investment.

Nike Class B stock jumped $3.50 to $63.50 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active issues on volume of more than 2.7 million shares. On Tuesday the stock, which has been battered this year by concerns about slowing growth in its core U.S. footwear market, gained $3.75.

Traders said they believed Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. had used its GEICO insurance company as the vehicle to buy into Nike, which last month hit a recent low of $51.25 a share, down from more than $76 in February.

One trader said the Berkshire interest in Nike likely came not from Buffett himself but from Louis Simpson, president and chief executive officer of GEICO Capital Operations, Buffett's often-rumoured heir apparent.
Buffett's office and GEICO declined to comment, while a Nike spokesman said the reports were "purely speculative."
"We have received no verification that that is indeed the case," said Nike spokesman Vada Manager.
Berkshire Hathaway would have to file with the Securities and Exchange Commission if it accumulated 5 percent or more of Nike. The filing would have to be made within 10 days.

Despite the stock's 12 percent surge over two days, industry analysts said Beaverton, Ore.-based Nike was expected to remain under short-term pressure due to the concerns about the U.S. footwear market.

"The athletic footwear sector in general in the United States has shown a couple of months of somewhat disappointing results," said Mike Kahn of Gruntal & Co., one of several analysts who has downgraded the stock in recent months.
He said that while Nike was still benefiting from its rapidly growing clothing sales and booming overseas markets, overall growth was slowing after two superheated years.

Nike's fiscal year ends on Saturday and the company is expected to report revenues of $9.5 billion, up nearly 50 percent from last year's $6.5 billion, said Kahn. He predicted fiscal 1998 revenues would rise a more modest 20 percent.

Nike profits are expected to follow the same pattern. For the fiscal year ending May 31, Nike earnings are expected to rise 52 percent to $2.84 a share, up from $1.87 a year ago, according to First Call, which tracks estimates. For fiscal 1998 earnings are expected to rise to $3.42 a share.

Julie Maack, a portfolio manager at Crabbe Huson Group Inc. in Portland, Ore., noted that Nike's target is to generate 50 percent of its business outside the United States within four years, up from about 40 percent currently.
But after the company's rapid sales growth over the past two years, some investors are shying away. "It's a time of transition, more of an uncertain period," Maack said.
Some analysts remain bullish on the stock.

"What people are really forgetting about with this company is that apparel is a major driver and international is a major driver, and it's not over yet," said Jennifer Black Groves of Black & Co., a Portland brokerage firm. "Anyone who plans to buy the stock for the long term will make a lot of money."
She said an investment by Buffett would make sense because of Nike's worldwide brand dominance and because Buffett likes out-of-favour stocks.
